title: Lost generation: the AI threat to Britain’s next great directors
key_facts: Commercials have long trained British directors such as Ridley Scott and Guy Ritchie; the article says the rush to AI in advertising raises fears of a 'lost generation'.
Luke Scott, who runs the group including Ridley Scott Associates, says he has fears and warns of the 'monoculturalisation of everything'.
WPP opened a flagship AI-enabled production facility in east London last month, the first in an international rollout of its £600m WPP Production business.
WPP CEO Cindy Rose says AI ushers in a 'golden age of marketing'; one unnamed industry source says some ads can be made up to 60% cheaper.
WPP Production chief executive Richard Glasson says AI is an enabler of abundance and that in production he sees jobs growing, not shrinking, and that big-budget ads will continue.
quote_evidence: But the panicked race to introduce AI technology across the advertising industry, to cut client costs and avoid being pushed aside by big tech, has raised fears of a lost generation who may be denied the opportunity to develop into great British film and TV directors.
One industry source said that some ads can be made up to 60% cheaper, which has some clients embracing AI-led ads to “show finance directors they are making savings”
“The elephant in the room is whether AI is coming for jobs, in production we are seeing the opposite.
why_it_matters_hint: Entry-level commercial work is where directors learn; AI could remove it.
notes: Feature with named and unnamed voices; the 60% cost figure comes from an unnamed industry source.
